subject: SLA request — latency spike and inference timeouts on 2027-06-20
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@frontierai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@frontierai.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Production outage 2027-06-20 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Hi Vanessa,

We experienced a sustained latency spike and intermittent inference timeouts impacting our production traffic between ~10:25–11:05 PDT today. Timeouts caused ~7% of requests to fail and several customer-facing flows degraded. Our SRE collected traces and flagged the issue to your status page (we cross-referenced the incident id).

Can you confirm whether this incident meets Redwood's SLA credit eligibility and, if so, provide a preliminary estimate of a service credit? We need an approximate number for our finance team and to include on our weekly executive report.

PO/references: FrontierAI PO 98765, Support ticket #78421 (attached).

Thanks — appreciate a quick acknowledgment and next steps.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Platform Engineering Manager
FrontierAI
samir.p@frontierai.com

Attachments: support-ticket-#78421.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@frontierai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage 2027-06-20 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and the ticket. I'm very sorry FrontierAI saw that impact. We saw a correlated frontend service overload in our metrics and we've already pulled the initial logs. Connor from Ops is looped in to validate the timeline and quantification; Marissa from Billing will own the credit issuance workflow.

Next steps:
- Connor will confirm exact downtime/partial-degradation windows and attach the raw request logs (we'll include latency histograms + error-rate snapshots).
- Marissa will prepare a draft credit calculation using our standard SLA formula and share the spreadsheet for your review.
- I'll own communications and provide an ETA for issuance once approvals are complete.

Can you confirm the precise timezone you want us to use for reporting (your ticket lists UTC but your operations team is PDT)? Also confirm any blackout dates for credits (quarter-end accounting constraints).

We expect to get Connor's timeline within 24 hours and a draft credit calc by EOD Thursday.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@frontierai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage 2027-06-20 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Vanessa / Samir — I pulled the request logs and rolling-aggregated latency histograms. Short summary:
- Incident window: 2027-06-20 10:25:17 PDT – 2027-06-20 11:04:58 PDT (39m 41s)
- Error spike: 6.8% of requests returned 504/timeout during the window
- Median latency during window: 820ms (baseline median 120ms)

I've attached the raw log excerpt (incident-frontend-latency-20270620.log) and a CSV of per-minute success rates. Based on the service contract, the useful metric is percent uptime over the billing period; we'll calculate the proportional credit following the SLA formula in section 4.2 (service outage compensation).

I'll hand this to Marissa for the calc. Samir, if you have any additional traces (client-side retries) please upload them to the Drive link — it helps us verify user impact.

--Connor
Connor O'Brien
Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-frontend-latency-20270620.log

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@frontierai.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage 2027-06-20 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Hi all — I ran the preliminary SLA credit calc using the standard formula: credit = (downtime minutes / total minutes in billing period) * monthly fee cap (per contract language). For FrontierAI's June billing window and the incident window Connor provided, the draft numbers are below. I've attached the working spreadsheet (credit-calculation-frontierai-20270624.xlsx) with line-by-line assumptions.

Draft summary (pre-approval):
- Billing period: June 1–30, 2027 (30 days = 43,200 minutes)
- Incident downtime-equivalent minutes: 39.68 minutes
- Calculated service availability reduction: 0.0918%
- Contracted monthly service fee (per invoice/PO 98765): $150,000
- Draft credit amount: $137.70 (rounded) — note our credit floor policy: credits under $250 are issued as account credit on next invoice unless customer requests check/ACH.

Questions for FrontierAI:
- Would you prefer an account credit on next invoice (default) or a separate refund/ACH?
- Any reason this needs escalation to finance for an exception (i.e., immediate cash refund)?

If no objections, I will route this to Finance for approval and prepare the accounting memo. Assuming standard approval path, issuance should appear on your account within 30 days (next invoice cycle). If FrontierAI needs a faster route, tell us and we'll escalate.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: credit-calculation-frontierai-20270624.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@frontierai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@frontierai.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage 2027-06-20 — request for SLA credit eligibility

Thanks — and thanks to the team for the quick turnaround. The draft calculation looks reasonable. FrontierAI prefers the issuance as an account credit on the next invoice. No need for an immediate cash refund.

One minor ask: can you include the accounting memo or a simple one-page statement we can attach to our GL for audit purposes? It should show: incident window, downtime minutes, calculation summary, and that credit will be applied to invoice July 1. Also, please confirm the HubSpot ticket/deal id for our records.

If you can provide the one-pager, we're good to close the loop on our side.

— Samir
